text:
Maria: Thinking aloud — we need a principled approach for connection priority + fairness when edge pools are saturated. Current behavior just accepts streams until OOM/queue blowup. Proposal: introduce a degradable SLA tier for streaming that can be downgraded to batched non-streaming or preempted after an inactivity window.

Sam: +1 on explicit degradable tier. Do you mean preempt mid-stream (kill) or convert to non-streaming response?

Maria: Prefer convert when possible (emit final tokens via a single response). Kill only if conversion isn't compatible (e.g., long-lived tool streams). Conversion avoids client-side replays.

Devon: Conversion requires checkpointing the KV-cache and ability to resume from a token checkpoint on a different backend. We only have partial support today. Also need an abort signal semantics: `X-Edge-Preempt: attempt-convert` vs `X-Edge-Preempt: kill`.

Zach: Gateway changes needed: 1) mark stream as "degradable" at admission time, 2) attach preempt-policy header, 3) allow backend to emit a `conversion-ready` trailer with a final chunk. Also we need to surface `streaming_mode: partial->final` in telemetry.

Katie: Before we change infra, what metrics will prove this helps? Suggested: tail-latency delta for high-priority reqs, number of midstream kills, number of conversions, and per-customer aborted-stream rate.

Maria: Good set. Add per-pool memory pressure gauge + preempt-trigger count. Run canary for 2 weeks targeting a single busy pool.

Sam: Implementation idea: token-based fairness. Each connection gets a credit bucket that refills by `credits/sec` weighted by SLA. If bucket < threshold, stream enters "consolidated mode" (server buffers small chunks and emits at batched cadence) or flips to degrade path.

Devon: Token buckets work, but watch bursty interactive flows — they might deplete then spike and get killed. Suggest soft-grace: allow one full burst per minute. Also track `last_active_client_seq` to avoid killing active writers.

Zach: Edge/Proxy API sketch:
```yaml
preempt_policy:
  mode: degrade|kill
  grace_burst: 1m
  credit_rate: 50 tokens/s
  convert_timeout_ms: 15000
```
Gateway will attach `x-edge-preempt` with JSON blob for debugging.

Katie: UX for SDKs — if we convert to final non-stream, client must handle a `converted: true` flag and stop expecting trailers. We'll need SDK bumps and changelog.

Maria: Action items: 1) Zach/Devon to propose minimal wire changes + backward compatibility plan (due EOD Tue). 2) Sam to prototype fairness token algorithm (bench with synthetic 5k conns). 3) Katie to draft metric dashboard and SLOs. I'll open an RFC follow-up with these details.

ingress-bot: RFC follow-up created: RFC-2026-edge-degrade-paths (staging). Link: https://go/redwood/rfc/2026 :bookmark_tabs: 

Sam: quick perf note — conversion will increase p95 CPU on conversion code path, we should budget a small reserved headroom per pool.

Devon: Also confirm state purge behavior: if conversion fails, backend should still send `x-edge-failure-reason` in trailer so gateway can decide to retry/kill.

Zach: Will add trailer conventions. Also thinking about experiments: A/B test degrade vs kill on 10% of traffic to observe client impact.

Katie: Sounds good. I'll sync with docs + SDK owners after RFC lands.

Maria: Thanks all. Small followup: label this "degradable-stream" feature so product can map to pricing tiers. :thumbsup:
